result.summary: Reionization ionizing-photon-budget reconciliation at z~8: star-forming galaxies require f_esc=0.247 (+0.248/-0.126) to close the budget (Madau-Dickinson SFRD, log xi_ion=25.5+/-0.15, clumping C=2-5, JWST-SFRD tail), versus indirect-proxy-inferred f_esc=0.050 (+0.076/-0.030) from LzLCS O32/beta calibrations. Median delta(required-inferred)=+0.181 dex-frac (16-84%: +0.043 to +0.429); 91% of the systematic MC shows a shortfall. Conclusion: a genuine SHORTFALL remains, and the sign holds under both O32 and beta calibrations. The result is bounded by the xi_ion x clumping x proxy-calibration systematic, not by statistics.
result.title: A residual reionization ionizing-photon-budget shortfall for star-forming galaxies at z~8 (beta systematic corner)
result.provenance: Literature-anchored budget calculation — NO survey catalog data is used. The cosmic SFRD is the Madau & Dickinson (2014) analytic fitting function; xi_ion and the O32/beta f_esc proxy calibrations are adopted published values (LzLCS: Chisholm+22, Flury+22; Simmonds+24). Do NOT state or imply that this study uses JWST, SDSS, or TNG observational/catalog data — it is a systematics reconciliation over published literature values.
result.review:
VERDICT: MINOR

The manuscript provides a thorough analysis of the reionization-photon-budget using existing literature values, but there are some minor concerns that require attention. The top correctness/overclaim risks include potential overreliance on indirect proxy calibrations and assumptions about clumping factors, which may introduce uncertainties in the results. Missing caveats could involve a more detailed discussion of how variations in galaxy properties and environments might affect the photon budget calculations.

The single most important fix is to provide a clearer explanation of how the systematic Monte Carlo simulations were conducted, including details on the input parameters and assumptions made. This will help strengthen the robustness of the conclusions drawn from these simulations. Overall, the manuscript presents a well-structured argument but requires minor adjustments to address these concerns before publication.

While relevant to the broader topic of reionization and photon budget, they do not specifically report measuring the reionization-photon-budget using JWST data.

Given this analysis, none of the papers explicitly report measuring the reionization-photon-budget via an ionizing-photon-budget method using JWST data as proposed. While some papers touch on related aspects (photon budget crisis, galaxies' ionizing properties during reionization), they either use different datasets or do not specifically focus on the measurement proposed.
